note: The paths are the ones a Supabase project answers on. The reference here is not a binary anybody can download: storage-api ships as an image, so the recording is taken from the one supabase start brings up, at the version in versions.json.
Buckets only. The object surface needs a case to be able to carry bytes and a target to have somewhere to put them, and neither is true yet.

The fixture pins what it wrote, so a reading case is compared byte for byte. A case that makes a bucket cannot pin what the server is about to write, so those name their timestamps in volatile and the rest of the answer is still compared whole.

Every case that changes a row says so, and the rows go back before it runs. The reading cases are written before the writing ones inside each feature for the same reason: a read after a write would be asked about whatever the write left.

A case with no key at all is asking the gateway rather than the storage server, which matters because zou is both and the reference is neither: the image runs behind kong in a local project, and kong is what answers a request with no apikey.
